newsitem.title: UK: ITV welcomes move to keep C4 funding for 1998.
newsitem.headline: ITV welcomes move to keep C4 funding for 1998.

text.p: The UK's Independent Television Association (ITV) said on Monday it welcomed the British government's decision to retain the Channel 4 television funding formula for 1998.
Earlier today, Britain's Department of Trade & Industry said that the current government funding formula used to run Channel 4 would end by 1999.

The DTI quoted British culture secretary Chris Smith as saying that there was no need, or real justification for the C4 formula now that it was a well-established broadcaster with a steady income stream.
ITV chairman Leslie Hill said that the government's decision recognised the difficulties the ITV companies would have faced if the funding formula had been discontinued from next year.
"The decision will mitigate the financial impact on the ITV companies by providing a smoother transition to 1999," said Hill.

Channel 4 said earlier that it welcomed the government's move to end its current funding formula and said it would spend more money on commissioning original British programmes and on further training of staff.
